Admission.description: Whether state-writing runs require a CI deployment admission.

DeletionPolicy.description: What happens to a unit's resources when it leaves the ownership set.

DriftRepair.description:
Whether reconcile repairs drift on its own.

Contract: [Drift](../../../../design/orchestration-core.md#drift).

oneOf.description:
The next reconcile executes drifted units whose recovery policy is
`converge` again; a drifted unit that is not safe to re-run awaits
approval.

Reconcile repairs no drift by itself: drifted units stay `drifted`
until `nyl reconcile --unit <unit> --reapply --reason <text>`.

EnvironmentSource.description:
The source commit of an environment's runs: a ref whose tip each run uses,
optionally pinned to a commit that `nyl update source-locks` moves, or the
commit the newest promotion recorded.

commit.description: Full 40-character lowercase commit ID that is read, refreshed by `nyl update source-locks`.

fromPromotion.description: The source commit recorded by the newest promotion on a path; excludes the other fields.

repository.description: Inline repository coordinates to read from. Mutually exclusive with `repositoryRef`.

repositoryRef.description: Project-local `gitops.nyl/v1` GitRepository to read from. Mutually exclusive with inline `repository`.

revision.description: Human-readable branch or tag that `nyl update source-locks` resolves.

EnvironmentState.description: The location of an environment's state: a repository and the refs within it.

admissionRef.description: Ref of the deployment admission record. Default the desired ref.

coordinationRefPrefix.description: Prefix, ending in `/`, of the leases, runs, and signals refs. Default `refs/nyl/`.

desiredRef.description: Ref of the desired state. A short name is a branch. Default `nyl/<environment>/desired`.

observedRef.description: Ref of the observed state; may equal `desiredRef`. Default `nyl/<environment>/observed`.

path.description: Directory of the environment's state within its refs, so several environments can share one ref. Default the root.

repository.description: Inline repository coordinates holding the state. Mutually exclusive with `repositoryRef`.

repositoryRef.description: GitRepository holding the state, read through its `repoURL` and written through its `publishURL`. Mutually exclusive with `repository`. Omitted with `repository`: the group's, else the checkout's `origin`, else the local repository.

EnvironmentTemplateSpec.description: The Environment's fields, templated, plus what only instances have.

admission.description: CI deployment admission: `required` makes state-writing runs use the source of the current admission. Omitted, `off`.

allowTeardown.description: Whether omission teardown needs no `--allow-teardown`: a unit removed from the template or its selection is torn down by the next reconcile. Default `false`.

allowUnprotectedSource.description: Whether runs may use source commits outside `protectedRefs`; previews run from pull request branches and set `true`. Omitted, `false`.

attestations.description: Environment-wide attestations, recorded with `nyl attest` for an instance's current state.

deletionPolicy.description: `Teardown` overrides every unit's own policy, including an explicit `Retain`, for the kinds that support teardown; units of other kinds are left in place and dropped from state when the instance is removed. `Retain` or omitted leaves each unit's own policy.

driftRepair.description: Whether `reconcile` repairs drift by itself. Omitted, `converge`.

keepSource.description: Opt in to keeping each instance's recorded source commit fetchable with a keep ref of its own, `refs/nyl-keep/<keepId>/<commit>`, in the source repository, for instances that may expire (`ttl`) long after their pull request branches are gone. `nyl state delete` removes the refs. Needs push access to `refs/nyl-keep/*` in the source repository, which a read-only token (GitHub's default `contents: read`, a fork pull request) lacks: without it `state init --template` and `reconcile --template` refuse (`NYL-INSTANCE-KEEP-FAILED`), so grant the access or leave `false`. Omitted, `false`: tear an instance down in the pull request closed job, which fetches the recorded commit by its id from the project's origin; GitHub keeps `refs/pull/<n>/head` and GitLab `refs/merge-requests/<n>/head` after the branch is deleted.

maxInstances.description: The most instances of this template that may exist at once, expired ones included until they are removed. At the limit, `state init --template` and `reconcile --template` refuse to create another instance (exit 2) and name the expired instances that could be removed; `--make-room` removes them first, oldest expiry first and only as many as needed. Needs `state.path` ending in `{{ environment.name }}` so Nyl can list the instances. Omitted, unlimited.

parameters.description: Typed parameters of an instance, exposed to templates as `params`; `--param <name>=<value>` parses its value as YAML and checks it against the declaration. A parameter without a `default` is required.

protectedRefs.description: Refs that pinned commits and run source commits must be reachable from. Omitted, the group's, else each repository's default branch.

source.description: The source commit runs use, which may template `revision` from `params`. Omitted, an instance runs from the commit recorded when it was created or last reconciled from a checkout.

state.description: Where an instance's state lives. Strings may read `environment.name` only. With `path` such as `{{ environment.name }}`, every instance shares the refs, one directory each.

ttl.description: How long an instance lives without activity, such as `7d`: `state init --template`, `reconcile --template`, and every other `reconcile` of the instance (unless `--no-extend`) move its `expiresAt` to now plus `ttl`. A `reconcile` that finds the instance expired removes it, the way `nyl state delete --teardown` does, unless it is `--renew` or `reconcile --template`; `reconcile --template <name>` without an instance sweeps every instance of the template and never extends. Omitted, instances never expire.

unitSelector.description: Matches literal unit `metadata.labels` across all unit kinds. An empty selector selects every unit.

values.description: Values unit templates see as `values`, with every string rendered as a template over `params` and `environment.name` when an instance is created.

GitOpsResourceMetadata.description: Metadata shared by local GitOps compiler resources.

labels.description: Literal labels used for organization and target selection.

name.description: Project-local identity, validated by the resource kind; remains static during discovery.

publishURL.description: Optional Git write URL. Publication uses `repoURL` when omitted.

repoURL.description: Credential-free Git read URL used by renderers and generated Applications.

InputDeclaration.description: One typed input a Release declares. Templates read its effective value as `inputs.<name>`.

default.description: Value used when the target binds none. Makes the input optional; must satisfy `type` and `enum`.

description.description: Documentation, surfaced in errors and inspection.

enum.description: Allowed values, for scalar types only. A non-empty list of values of the declared type.

InputType.description: Declared input type. Every type is a subset of JSON Schema.

oneOf.description: A JSON integer; numbers with a fractional part are rejected.
A JSON object. Only the top-level type is checked.
A JSON array. Only the top-level type is checked.

matchLabels.description: Exact label matches, combined with AND. An empty map selects every ApplicationGroup.

name.description: Project-local name of the referenced resource; its kind and API group are determined by the containing field.

PromotedSource.description: A source that promotion paths supply.

path.description: The PromotionPath that supplies the source. Mutually exclusive with `paths`.

paths.description: Several PromotionPaths; the newest record on any of them wins. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

promoted.description: The record `nyl promote` writes here with `record: source`, never by hand.

ReadGitRepository.description: Credential-free coordinates for a repository that is only read.

repoURL.description: Git read URL. Source checkouts never publish to this repository.

description:
What a preview environment looks like, instantiated with parameters.

Instances are created with `nyl state init --template` (or
`nyl reconcile --template`), exist only in state, and behave like declared
environments for every command. The template has the Environment's fields
plus `parameters`, `deletionPolicy`, `allowTeardown`, `ttl`,
`maxInstances`, and `keepSource`. Strings in `values`, `state`, and `source`
are templates: they read `params` and `environment.name` when an instance
is created from the template, and `state` reads only `environment.name`,
because it locates the state that holds the parameters.

## When needed

To give every pull request its own environment, created and removed by CI.

## If omitted

Every environment is declared with an `Environment` resource in source.

apiVersion.description: API group and version defining this resource.

kind.description: Resource kind within the API group.

metadata.description: Resource identity and metadata. Instances take its labels.
